owner_and_capability: Identity & Access — operator identity and refresh sessions behind operator login, refresh, MFA lockout and session revocation; Audit — operator action ledger; owner account queries for People Directory, Care Plan parent and CLI reads
atomic_cutover: The retained operator and refresh-token repository contracts become adapters over the public Identity & Access capability and the platform audit repository over the Audit appender; the old platform repositories are deleted in the same change. Foreign auth.accounts and auth.tokens reads use owner queries bound at construction. The legacy parent-account model, routes and client stay unchanged because auth.accounts_parents has no target owner. No dual provider or fallback read chain.
tests: Owner operator lifecycle, MFA lockout, rotation hand-off, revocation and expiry sweep; injected failure after each authoritative refresh write and after revocation, each with rollback proof and idempotent retry; platform-wide visibility from two tenant contexts; observation row counts; adapter contract tests preserving the retained (nil, nil) and DatabaseError shapes; platform-scoped audit ledger; fail-closed owner lookups; existing operator login/MFA/refresh/session-validation, parent dashboard and staff messaging suites; route goldens and architecture, composition and query-budget ratchets.

runtime_evidence.workload: 2026-09-10 local isolated PostgreSQL 17.11 clone, Go 1.27.0 darwin/arm64; five warmups plus 30 sequential login, refresh and revoke sequences over the public capability, refresh and revoke inside one administrative transaction each.
runtime_evidence.thresholds: No task-specific latency SLO or query budget is defined. Existing architecture, composition, query-budget and behavior gates apply; measured values are observations, not fitted thresholds or a production performance claim.
runtime_evidence.query_count: Login 3 statements and 2 DML rows; refresh 9 statements and 2 DML rows; revoke 4 statements and 2 DML rows, identical across all samples.
runtime_evidence.errors: 0/30 errors per operation; 70 commits and zero rollback events including warmups.
runtime_evidence.lock_wait: 70 lock-acquisition statement events totalling 21.724 ms including warmups. The hook measures SQL acquisition duration, an upper bound on lock wait; the workload is sequential and contains no contention, so these are a floor rather than load evidence.
runtime_evidence.failure: A failure is injected after each of the four authoritative writes of a refresh in turn and after family revocation; every case preserves the predecessor un-rotated, leaves no successor, keeps the family ending at the predecessor and records no login stamp. A second rotation hand-off returns the stable ErrOperatorSessionRotated error; rotated predecessors are retained as replay evidence until expiry.
runtime_evidence.rollback: Session, login and revocation writes roll back with the caller's administrative transaction; the full retry then commits, and a repeated revoke deletes nothing instead of failing.
runtime_evidence.smoke: Operator login, MFA, refresh replay and password-change revocation suites, four-portal session validation, parent dashboard listing, staff messaging reachability, cleanup CLI preview and the regenerated route goldens pass.
runtime_evidence.latency_p50: Login 0.778 ms; refresh 2.279 ms; revoke 0.832 ms (nearest rank over 30 samples).
runtime_evidence.latency_p95: Login 1.085 ms; refresh 3.126 ms; revoke 1.172 ms (nearest rank over 30 samples).
runtime_evidence.affected_rows: Two DML rows per operation: login inserts the session and stamps the login, refresh inserts the successor and marks the predecessor rotated, revoke deletes the family. Duplicate-prevention conflicts do not apply: no operator or session write is an upsert or conflict-tolerant insert, and the one conflict-shaped case, a repeated rotation hand-off, is rejected with the stable ErrOperatorSessionRotated error rather than absorbed.
runtime_evidence.pool_wait: Zero pool waits in the measured samples; 70 pool-wait events totalling 0.044 ms including warmups.
runtime_evidence.deadlocks: The database deadlock counter changed by zero and no transaction reported a retry, so there were no serialization retries.
runtime_evidence.job_duration: Not applicable: this capability has no Worker path.
runtime_evidence.job_retries: Not applicable: this capability has no Worker path.
runtime_evidence.job_backlog: Not applicable: this capability has no Worker path.

rollback_and_cleanup: Revert the composition and adapters against unchanged table shapes; no schema change and no irreversible cleanup.
exit_criterion: Every listed entry point reaches platform.operators, platform.operator_refresh_tokens, platform.operator_audit_log, auth.accounts and auth.tokens through one owner provider; scripts/backend-architecture.sh check introduces no key and leaves policy ownership unchanged. Partial delivery: thirteen of the sixteen listed keys were still in the baseline at the base commit and eleven are removed here; the two database/repositories/iot keys and database/repositories/platform|auth.accounts were already resolved by earlier waves. The database/repositories/auth keys auth.accounts_parents and auth.Where remain with the unchanged parent-account repository, so #2720 stays open.
